evidence_items.publisher: INFORMS / Management Science, abstract deposited with Crossref
evidence_items.explanation: The abstract reports a pooled 26.08% increase in completed tasks across three workplace experiments involving 4,867 developers. The original paper dates the experiments to 2022–2023; this is meaningful workplace enhancement, although task counts do not establish overall software quality or profitability.

A randomized study of 16 experienced developers working on familiar repositories found slower completion with early-2025 tools. This supports skepticism about benefits in that setting, but cannot establish that meaningful enhancement has never occurred elsewhere.

METR cautions that selection effects and measurement problems make its follow-up an unreliable estimate of current productivity effects. The early slowdown should therefore not be presented as a settled estimate for July 2026 tools.

unresolved_gaps: No usable representative accounting establishes what fraction of total coding-tool costs is hidden or paid by employers.
The evidence does not establish broad worker replacement.
Completed-task gains do not fully measure software quality, maintenance burden or financial returns.
